'''Friedrich Götze''' (born 6 August 1951 in [[Hameln]]) is a German mathematician, specializing in [[probability theory]], [[mathematical statistics]], and [[number theory]].

== Education and career ==
Götze studied mathematics and physics at the [[University of Göttingen]] and the [[University of Bonn]] by means of a scholarship from the [[Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes]].<ref>{{cite book|editor=Peter Eichelsbacher|editor2=Guido Elsner|editor3=Holger Kösters|editor4=Matthias Löwe|editor5=Franz Merkl|editor6=Silke Rolles|title=Limit Theorems in Probability, Statistics and Number Theory: In Honor of Friedrich Götze|chapter=''A Conversation with Friedrich Götze'' by Willem R. van Zwet|isbn=978-3-642-36067-1|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vbZGAAAAQBAJ&pg=PA1|pages=1–22|date=7 May 2013|publisher=Springer }} {{cite book|title=eBook|isbn=978-3-642-36068-8|last1=Eichelsbacher|first1=Peter|last2=Elsner|first2=Guido|last3=Kösters|first3=Holger|last4=Löwe|first4=Matthias|last5=Merkl|first5=Franz|last6=Rolles|first6=Silke|date=23 April 2013|publisher=Springer }}</ref> In 1978 he received his doctorate from the [[University of Cologne]] with thesis ''Asymptotic Expansions in the Central Limit Theorem in Banach Spaces'' under the supervision of [[Johann Pfanzagl]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=23672}}</ref> At the University of Cologne, Götze was an assistant, interrupted by a year as visiting professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. In 1983 he [[Habilitation|habilitated]] in Cologne with thesis ''Asymptotic developments in central limit theorems''. In 1984 he became a professor of mathematics at [[Bielefeld University]]. For the academic years 1990/91 and 2002/2003 he was Dean of the Faculty of Mathematics.<ref name=Leopoldina>[http://idw-online.de/pages/de/news?print=1&id=349825 Professor Friedrich Götze Mitgleid der Leopoldina]</ref>

Götze is a member of the scientific advisory board of the [[Weierstrass Institute for Applied Analysis and Stochastics|Weierstrass Institute]] (of which he is a founding member) and of the board of the Gesellschaft für Mathematische Forschung, which supports and legally represents the [[Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach]].<ref>[http://www.mfo.de/about-the-institute/structure/society Gesellschaft für Mathematische Forschung e.V.]</ref> He is a Fellow of the [[University of Göttingen]]'s Institute for Mathematical Stochastics. He was in 2017/18 the vice-president and was elected for 2019/20 the president of the [[German Mathematical Society|Deutsche Mathematiker-Vereinigung]] (DMV).<ref>[https://www.mathematik.de/dmv-blog/334-praesidium-waehlt-dmv-praesidenten-und-vize-2017-18 Präsidium wählt DMV-Präsidenten und Vize (2017/18)]</ref>

== Research ==
His research deals with asymptotic methods, convergence rates and limit theorems in mathematical statistics, [[Markov process]]es, stochastic algorithms, probability theory, functional analysis, and spectral distribution in [[Random matrix|random matrices]].<ref>{{Cite journal |arxiv = 0709.3995|doi = 10.1214/09-AOP522|title = The circular law for random matrices|journal = The Annals of Probability|volume = 38|issue = 4|pages = 1444–1491|year = 2010|last1 = Götze|first1 = Friedrich|last2 = Tikhomirov|first2 = Alexander|s2cid = 1290255}}</ref> He applied probabilistic methods to [[analytic number theory]] and the geometry of numbers, including the problem of distribution and density of lattice points in ellipses. With the introduction of fundamental new methods, he gave a new, effective proof of the [[Oppenheim conjecture]], which was first proved by [[Grigory Margulis]] in 1987.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Bentkus, Vidmantas|author2=Götze, Friedrich|title=Lattice point problems and distribution of values of quadratic forms|journal=Annals of Mathematics|volume=150|issue=3|year=1999|pages=977–1027 |arxiv=math/9911261|doi=10.2307/121060|jstor=121060|bibcode=1999math.....11261B|s2cid=15726252}}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Buterus, Paul|author2=Götze, Friedrich|author3=Hille, Thomas|author4=Margulis, Gregory|title=Distribution of Values of Quadratic Forms at Integral Points|eprint=1004.5123|year=2010|class=math.NT}}</ref>
Götze was the spokesperson for the [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft|DFG]] Collaborative Research Center's ''Spektrale Strukturen und Topologische Methoden in der Mathematik'' (Spectral Structures and Topological Methods in Mathematics).<ref name=Leopoldina/>

== Honors and awards ==
Götze was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin in 1988.<ref>{{cite book|author=Götze, Friedrich|chapter=Lattice point problems and the central limit theorem in Euclidean spaces|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. III|year=1998|pages=245–255|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011582000}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Götze, F.|chapter=Errata to: ''Lattice point problems and the central limit theorem in Euclidean spaces''|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. I|year=1998|page=648|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011746000}}</ref> In 2009 he became a member of the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|Leopoldina]].<ref name=Leopoldina/> In 2012 he was the [[Gauss Lectureship|Gauss Lecturer]] with talk ''Der mehrdimensionale zentrale Grenzwertsatz und die Geometrie der Zahlen'' (The multidimensional central limit theorem and the geometry of numbers). For his contribution to the establishment of the [[European Institute for Statistics, Probability, Stochastic Operations Research and its Applications]] (Eurandom), he was awarded the [[Order of Orange-Nassau]] in 2014.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nw-news.de/owl/11228626_Niederlaendischer_Koenig_ehrt_Bielefelder_Mathematiker.html|title=Niederländischer König ehrt Bielefelder Mathematiker (Dutch King honors Bielefeld mathematician)|newspaper=Neue Westfälische (newspaper)|date=28 August 2014}}</ref>
